items.title: unitycatalog-rs
items.text:
A Rust reimplementation of Unity Catalog OSS, the open catalog for data and AI. It has upstream's REST APIs (Unity Catalog, Delta and Iceberg REST), a web UI, the uc CLI and a Python client. It keeps the catalog in an embedded database (Turso) or in PostgreSQL.

pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[all]'
uc dev

Quickstart Install

  • Server

    Run uc-server on your machine, in Docker or on Kubernetes. Keep the catalog in PostgreSQL, sign users in, and give clients credentials for S3, ADLS and GCS.

    Run the server

  • Clients

    The uc CLI and its terminal UI, the Python client, the web UI, and the REST APIs for engines such as Polars, deltalake and PyIceberg.

    Use the clients

  • Reference

    Each operation of the HTTP APIs, each class of the Python client, each command of uc, each setting and each value of the Helm chart.

    Look it up

  • Upstream

    Clients of upstream's server use this server as they are. The README compares the two servers, feature by feature.

    Compare

items.title: CLI
items.text:
uc has the commands of upstream's bin/uc, with the same flags, and more: a terminal UI, personal access tokens, backups, the Iceberg catalog, and a local server.

pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[cli]'
uc catalog list
uc catalog create --help

CLI commands lists every command and its flags.

items.title: Connect to a server
items.text:
uc calls http://localhost:8080 by default. For another server, give --server, set UC_CLI_SERVER, or write it in uc.toml:

# uc.toml, in this folder or a folder above it
[cli]
server = "https://uc.example.com"

--output json or --output jsonPretty prints JSON instead of a table.

items.title: Sign in
items.text:
When the server needs a sign-in:

uc auth login

uc auth login signs you in to your identity provider in your browser, and keeps the server's token for the next commands, until it expires (24 hours by default). It needs the provider's OAuth settings, oauth_* in [cli]. uc auth logout removes the sign-in.

For scripts, give a token with --auth_token or UC_CLI_TOKEN, such as a personal access token:

uc token create --name laptop

Without a token or a sign-in, uc signs in with the identity of the environment, as the Python client does: an Azure, Google or AWS identity, an OAuth client in UC_OAUTH_*, or a token in UC_TOKEN, at an identity provider that the server takes. A service principal, a pod or a CI job thus needs no uc auth login. uc auth and --auth_token, also --auth_token '', do not use that identity. uc auth login --access_token exchanges a provider's access token instead of an identity token, such as the one az account get-access-token --scope https://uc.example.com/.default prints.

items.title: Tables, volumes and functions
items.text:
uc table create --full_name main.default.events \
  --columns "id INT, name STRING" --storage_location /tmp/uc/events
uc table write --full_name main.default.events   # 15 random rows
uc table read --full_name main.default.events

uc volume create --full_name main.default.files --storage_location /tmp/uc/files
uc volume write --full_name main.default.files --source ./report.csv
uc volume read --full_name main.default.files --path report.csv

uc function create --full_name main.default.add \
  --input_params "a INT, b INT" --data_type INT --def "return a + b"
uc function call --full_name main.default.add --input_params "1,2"
  • uc table create writes a Delta table at the location. With --table_type MANAGED, the server chooses the location.
  • uc table and uc volume read and write with the server's temporary credentials: local paths, S3, ADLS and GCS.
  • uc function call runs the function on your machine, with python3.

items.title: Run a server
items.text:
Command What it does uc dev Runs uc-server on 127.0.0.1:8080, with the catalog in memory (unless db.url is set) and its managed data in .uc, and opens the web UI. uc serve Runs uc-server with its flags, such as --port. uc web Serves the web UI on http://localhost:3000, for the server of --server.

These need pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[server]', and [ui] for the web UI.

items.title: Differences from upstream's CLI
items.text:
• The settings are in uc.toml and UC_CLI_* variables, not in cli.properties.
  • uc with no command opens the terminal UI.
  • New commands: token, group, admin, iceberg, tui, serve, dev and web.

items.title: Python client
items.text:
The package unitycatalog-rs calls the server's APIs from Python, with or without asyncio. It imports as unitycatalog. It is generated from the server's API definitions, so it has a method for each route.

pip install unitycatalog-rs

Note

Its API is not the API of upstream's Python client, unitycatalog-client.

items.title: Connect
items.text:
from unitycatalog import Client

client = Client("http://localhost:8080/")

With sign-in, the client sends a bearer token with each request. It gets one in one of these ways:

  • The identity of the environment. Client(url) without a token signs in with what the environment has, at an identity provider that the server takes (Identity providers). Nothing in the code names it: the variables are the configuration, and moving from a laptop to a pod changes none of it.

    Identity What the environment has Azure service principal AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET Azure workload identity AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE Azure managed identity AZURE_CLIENT_ID for a user-assigned one, else IDENTITY_ENDPOINT or MSI_ENDPOINT Azure CLI az on the path, signed in, without the variables of a managed identity Google service account GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS Google Cloud CLI gcloud on the path, signed in Google machine or pod GCE_METADATA_HOST or K_SERVICE AWS access keys AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, with AWS_SESSION_TOKEN for temporary ones AWS web identity (EKS) AWS_ROLE_ARN, AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE AWS container (ECS, EKS Pod Identity) AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI or AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI AWS instance role (EC2) AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION Any OAuth client UC_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL, UC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, UC_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, with UC_OAUTH_SCOPE and UC_OAUTH_AUDIENCE when the provider needs them A token UC_TOKEN, or a file with one in UC_TOKEN_FILE

    The Azure and Google identities ask for a token for an audience of the server's issuer, so the server must list the provider with direct = true. An AWS identity signs a request for STS with the server id of the server's AWS block (AWS). The audience or server id is the one that UC_AUDIENCE names, else the server's URL as the client calls it: the client asks for no other, so a server cannot have the identity sign for another service. The AWS CLI's profiles are not read: aws configure export-credentials --format env puts a profile's keys in the environment.

    Client(url) asks the server which providers it takes. A server that cannot answer yet is asked again at each call, and the calls go without a token until it answers.

  • A token provider. token_provider= names one: one of unitycatalog.identity, with the scope or audience of the server's issuer, or a callable that returns the token, or a pair of the token and when it expires, in seconds since the epoch. The callable runs on a thread of its own, one call at a time, so it can call the methods of a client.

    import time

from unitycatalog import Client, identity

Client(url, token_provider=identity.azure("https://uc.example.com/.default"))
Client(url, token_provider=identity.google("https://uc.example.com"))
Client(url, token_provider=identity.aws("https://uc.example.com"))
Client(url, token_provider=identity.client_credentials(token_url, client_id, client_secret))
Client(url, token_provider=lambda: (fetch_token(), time.time() + 3600))

  • A fixed token. token=: a personal access token, or a token of the server.

    import os

client = Client("https://uc.example.com/", token=os.environ["UC_TOKEN"])

items.title: Catalogs, schemas and tables
items.text:
client.create_catalog("main", comment="primary")
client.create_schema("default", "main")
print([catalog.name for catalog in client.list_catalogs()])

client.catalog("main").update(comment="the main catalog")
table = client.table("main.default.events").get()
client.catalog("main").delete(force=True)  # also deletes its schemas and tables
  • The arguments have the names of the REST API's fields. The required ones are positional, the others are keywords.
  • client.catalog(name), client.table(full_name) and the other handles have the requests on one object: get, update and delete.
  • The methods return classes, such as CatalogInfo and TableInfo, with each field as an attribute. They cannot change, and they compare by value.
  • The enums are enum.StrEnum classes: give TableType.MANAGED or "MANAGED".
  • The list methods return all the items, page after page. max_results limits them.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
from unitycatalog import NotFoundError

try:
    client.catalog("missing").get()
except NotFoundError as e:
    print(e.code, e.message)  # CATALOG_NOT_FOUND Catalog not found: missing

Each error is a UnityCatalogError, with a subclass per HTTP status, such as NotFoundError, PermissionDeniedError and ConflictError.

items.title: Async
items.text:
Each method that sends a request also comes as <name>_async:

catalog, schemas = await asyncio.gather(
    client.catalog("main").get_async(),
    client.list_schemas_async("main"),
)

items.title: Temporary credentials
items.text:
table = client.table("main.default.events").get()
credentials = client.generate_temporary_table_credentials(table.table_id, "READ")
aws = credentials.aws_temp_credentials
storage_options = {
    "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": aws.access_key_id,
    "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": aws.secret_access_key,
    "AWS_SESSION_TOKEN": aws.session_token,
}

Give these to a reader of the table, such as deltalake or Polars.

items.title: Files
items.text:
The server reads and writes the files of a volume, and reads the files of a table, so the client needs no storage credentials:

root = "/Volumes/main/default/landing"
client.upload_file(f"{root}/data/a.csv", b"id,name\n1,x\n", overwrite=True)
for entry in client.list_directory_contents(f"{root}/data").contents:
    print(entry.name, entry.file_size)
data = client.download_file(f"{root}/data/a.csv").contents
head = client.download_file(f"{root}/data/a.csv", range="bytes=0-1023").contents

See Files API.

items.title: Reference
items.text: The Python API lists every method, class and enum, with its arguments. help(Client.create_table) shows the same.

items.title: REST APIs
items.text:
The server has upstream's REST APIs, so clients of upstream's server use it as they are. The HTTP API reference shows each operation.

Base path API For /api/2.1/unity-catalog Unity Catalog REST API Catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, functions, models, grants and credentials. /api/2.1/unity-catalog/delta/v1 Delta REST API Managed Delta tables, from Delta 4.3 and delta-kernel-rs. /api/2.1/unity-catalog/iceberg/v1 Iceberg REST catalog Iceberg clients, such as PyIceberg. /api/v1/delta-sharing Delta Sharing Recipients of shares: tables. /api/1.0/opensharing Open Sharing Recipients of shares: tables, volumes and agent skills. /api/1.0/unity-control Control plane Token exchange, and SCIM users and groups. /api/2.0/fs Files API The files of volumes and, read-only, of tables, as the Databricks Files API has them.

With sign-in on, each request needs a token: Authorization: Bearer <token>. See Sign-in and authorization.

items.title: Unity Catalog REST API
items.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/2.1/unity-catalog/catalogs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name": "main"}'
curl http://localhost:8080/api/2.1/unity-catalog/catalogs

Lists take max_results and page_token, and answer with next_page_token when there are more results. Errors have upstream's body:

{"error_code": "CATALOG_NOT_FOUND", "message": "Catalog not found: missing"}

items.title: Iceberg REST catalog
items.text:
Each catalog is an Iceberg warehouse, and its schemas are the namespaces:

from pyiceberg.catalog import load_catalog

catalog = load_catalog(
    "uc",
    type="rest",
    uri="http://localhost:8080/api/2.1/unity-catalog/iceberg",
    warehouse="main",
)
print(catalog.list_namespaces())

The server gives the client temporary credentials for each table that it loads.

items.title: Files API
items.text:
The server reads and writes the files with the credentials of the volume or table, so the caller needs no storage credentials. A path is /Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/..., or /Tables/<catalog>/<schema>/<table>/... for the files of a table:

fs=http://localhost:8080/api/2.0/fs
curl -X PUT --data-binary @a.csv "$fs/files/Volumes/main/default/landing/data/a.csv?overwrite=true"
curl "$fs/directories/Volumes/main/default/landing/data"
curl -o a.csv "$fs/files/Volumes/main/default/landing/data/a.csv"
curl "$fs/directories/Tables/main/default/events/_delta_log"
Method Path Does GET /directories/<path> Lists a directory: contents, a page at a time (page_size, at most 1000, and page_token). HEAD /directories/<path> 200 when the directory exists. PUT /directories/<path> Creates a directory. DELETE /directories/<path> Deletes an empty directory; with recursive=true, a directory and what it holds. GET /files/<path> Downloads a file; takes a Range header. HEAD /files/<path> The file's Content-Length, Content-Type and Last-Modified. PUT /files/<path> Uploads the body as the file; overwrite=true replaces a file that is there. DELETE /files/<path> Deletes a file.
  • Privileges: reads need READ VOLUME on a volume or SELECT on a table, as their temporary credentials. Writes need READ VOLUME and WRITE VOLUME on the volume, or its ownership.
  • recursive is ours: the Databricks Files API deletes only empty directories.
  • Tables are read-only: a file written or deleted outside the table's commits would break the table, so writes under /Tables fail.
  • Directories: in object storage, a directory exists only through its files. Creating one there only checks the path, and a directory without files is not found. Local storage has real directories.
  • Databricks SDK: WorkspaceClient(...).files works for these calls. For a file of 50 MB or more, the SDK starts a multipart upload, which the server does not have. Set disable_experimental_files_api_client=True in the SDK's Config: it then sends each upload as one PUT.

items.title: Delta Sharing and Open Sharing
items.text:
/shares and /recipients, in the Unity Catalog REST API, make shares and recipients, in the shape of the Databricks sharing API. A share holds tables, volumes and agent skills. An agent skill is a volume with a SKILL.md file. A recipient reads its shares with its own token, which starts with dsr_:

  • /api/v1/delta-sharing is the Delta Sharing protocol, for clients such as delta-sharing and deltalake. It has the tables of a share. A query answers the files of a Delta table as URLs that the recipient reads for one hour at most.
  • /api/1.0/opensharing is the Open Sharing protocol. It has the tables too, and the volumes and agent skills, and it gives temporary read-only credentials for each.

An admin does these steps:

  1. POST /shares makes a share.
  2. PATCH /shares/{name} changes its objects, with updates: each has an action (ADD, UPDATE or REMOVE) and a data_object. The name of an object is its full name in the catalog, and shared_as (<schema>.<name>) is what the recipient sees. For a volume or an agent skill, the field is string_shared_as.
  3. POST /recipients makes a recipient. The answer has no token. It has an activation link, in tokens[].activation_url.
  4. PATCH /shares/{name}/permissions lets the recipient read the share: a change with the recipient as principal and SELECT in add, or in remove to end it.
  5. The admin sends the activation link to the recipient.

The recipient opens the link once, without sign-in, and gets the profile file of a Delta Sharing client, with the token. The link then stops working, and the server keeps a hash of the token only. POST /recipients/{name}/rotate-token makes a new token and a new link. The older tokens end at once, or after existing_token_expire_in_seconds. expiration_time of a recipient is when its tokens end.

A table in a share gives its latest version only. With history_data_sharing_status ENABLED, recipients read older versions too, by version or by time; start_version is the lowest version they read.

A share that a recipient was not granted answers 404, as a share that does not exist.

Limits

  • Delta tables only. A query has no change data feed (/changes) and no delta response format.
  • File URLs are for S3 and Azure. For Google Cloud Storage, recipients use the temporary credentials of the Open Sharing protocol.
  • A table under a local path answers file:// URLs, which only a recipient on the same machine can read.
  • A share object is a table, a volume or an agent skill. Partitions and cdf_enabled of an object, storage_root of a share and OAuth recipients are refused.
  • The answers of /shares and /recipients have their 64-bit numbers, such as created_at, as text.

items.title: Terminal UI
items.text:
uc with no command, or uc tui, opens a terminal UI. It has a tab for each kind of object, the list on the left, and the selected object, as JSON, on the right. It calls the server of the uc commands, with their sign-in.

uc
Key Action Tab, Shift+Tab Next or previous tab. Down, Up Select an item. Enter, Backspace Open the item, such as the schemas of a catalog; go back up. Page Down, Page Up Scroll the details. C Create an item. D Delete the item, after a question. R Load the list again. S Change the server. ? Show all keys. Q Quit.

On the tokens tab, C makes a personal access token. It shows once.

With only BROWSE on a catalog or an external location, you see the object and what it holds, with browse only after the name and in the title of the details. You see their metadata, not their data, and D does not delete them.

When you quit, the terminal UI keeps the server, the tab and the item that you opened, for the next start.

items.title: Web UI
items.text: The web UI shows the catalogs of a server, and creates, edits and deletes what they hold. It is a port of upstream's new console, with grants, temporary credentials, column comments, a page for your access tokens, and the pages under Manage. uc-server serves it at /.

items.title: Open it
items.text:
• uc dev runs a server with the UI, and opens it in your browser.
  • The image and the Helm chart serve the UI at /.
  • uc web serves the UI on http://localhost:3000, for another server (--server), with the token of uc.

When the server needs a sign-in, the UI shows its login page first: see Sign-in and authorization.

items.title: Use it
items.text:
• Catalogs, on the left, is the tree of catalogs, schemas, and the tables, metric views, volumes, functions and models of each schema. Click a name to open its page.
  • Each page has three tabs: Overview (the description and what the object holds), Details (its fields, properties and JSON) and Permissions. Volumes and tables also have Files.
  • Create: Create catalog on the list of catalogs, Create schema on a catalog, and New on a schema, for a table, metric view, volume, SQL function or registered model. A new table is managed, or external at a storage location, with any number of columns. The Iceberg REST catalog creates an Iceberg table, with its first metadata file.
  • Metric view: give its YAML definition, the full name of the table it reads, and one column for each dimension and measure of the YAML, with the same name. Its page shows the columns and the definition.
  • Edit: the button at the top of a page, or Edit on the description. The pencil in a column's row edits the column's comment.
  • Delete: the button at the top of a page; type the name to confirm. The server deletes only a catalog, schema, model or credential that holds nothing; an admin can tick a box to delete what it holds too.
  • Browse only: with only BROWSE on a catalog or an external location, you see the object and what it holds, with a Browse only badge. You see their names, comments, columns and other metadata, but no Files tab, no temporary credentials, no model versions and no buttons that change them.
  • The buttons at the right of the header choose the light theme, the dark theme or the system's.

items.title: Search
items.text:
The box in the header finds catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, functions and models by the words of their names and comments. Press / to go to it.

  • Type at least two characters: the first results show under the box. The arrow keys and Enter, or a click, open one.
  • See all results, or Enter without a marked result, opens the search page: all the results, with a tab for each type, and Load more for the next page.
  • Names equal to the text come first, then names that start with it, names that hold it, and the objects whose comment holds its words. You see only the objects that you may read or browse.
  • On Turso, a word matches anywhere in a word: rders finds sales_orders. On PostgreSQL, a word matches the start of a word: ord finds sales_orders, rders does not.

items.title: Files
items.text:
The Files tab of a volume or table shows the files in its storage location. Click a folder to open it, and a name in the path above the list to go back. The download button gets a file.

Click a file to view it. The viewer shows text, JSON (pretty-printed; for a Delta log, one document per line), CSV and TSV files as a table, and images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, BMP, AVIF, up to 10 MB). It reads a large file 512 KB at a time: scroll down for more, up to 10 MB. Parquet, Avro and other binary files have no preview: download them.

The owner of a volume also sees Upload (one or more files, with a box to replace files that are there), New folder, and a delete button in each row. For a folder that holds files, the dialog says what it holds; tick the box to delete them too. The files of a table are read-only. See Files API.

items.title: Permissions
items.text: The Permissions tab shows your privileges on the object and its grants. The owner and admins can grant a privilege to a user's email and revoke one with its ×. For tables, volumes and external locations, Vend READ creds and Vend READ WRITE creds show temporary credentials for the storage, as an engine gets them.

items.title: Manage
items.text:
Under the tree, Manage has the credentials and external locations, and, for admins, the users, groups and audit log:

  • Credentials: an AWS IAM role that the server assumes, an Azure service principal or managed identity that it signs in as, or a GCP service account or service account key, with the external locations bound to it.
  • External locations: a URL in cloud storage and its credential. See Cloud storage.
  • Users: create a user by email; Delete deletes the user, with its grants, access tokens and group memberships.
  • Groups: create a group, then add and remove its members on its page.
  • Audit log: the calls that changed the catalog, with a filter by principal, method, path and time. A signed-in admin sees it.

items.title: Access tokens
items.text:
An access token lets a script call the API as you. Click the avatar, then Access tokens:

  1. Click Create token, give a name, and choose when it expires.
  2. Click Copy, and keep the token safe: the page shows it only once.
  3. To stop a token, click Delete in its row.

items.title: Install
items.text:
unitycatalog-rs has four parts:

Part What it does uc-server Serves the REST APIs, and the web UI at /. uc Runs upstream's bin/uc commands, a terminal UI, and uc dev. Python client Calls the APIs from Python, with or without asyncio. Web UI Shows and changes the catalog in a browser.

items.title: pip
items.text:
The package unitycatalog-rs is the Python client. Its extras add the other parts, of the same version:

Install Adds pip install unitycatalog-rs The Python client only. pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[cli]' uc. pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[server]' uc-server and uc. pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[ui]' The web UI and uc. pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[all]' All of them.

The wheels are for Python 3.12 and later, and free-threaded Python 3.14t, on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64, glibc and musl), macOS (x86_64 and arm64) and Windows (x86_64).

items.title: Docker
items.text:
The image ghcr.io/open-lakehouse/unitycatalog-rs has uc-server, uc and the web UI:

docker run -d --name uc -p 8080:8080 -v uc-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/open-lakehouse/unitycatalog-rs:0.0.2

See Docker.

items.title: Helm
items.text:
The Helm chart runs the image on Kubernetes, with the catalog in PostgreSQL. Name your PostgreSQL server in values.yaml, as Kubernetes shows:

helm install uc oci://ghcr.io/open-lakehouse/charts/uc-server \
  --version 0.0.2 --namespace uc --create-namespace -f values.yaml

items.title: Quickstart
items.text: Run a server on your machine, make a table, and read it.

items.title: 1. Start a server
items.text:
pip install 'unitycatalog-rs[all]'
uc dev

This installs the server, the CLI, the Python client and the web UI. uc dev runs a server on http://localhost:8080, and opens the web UI in your browser. The server keeps the catalog in memory: it is gone when uc dev stops.

items.title: 2. Make a table
items.text:
In a second terminal:

uc catalog create --name main
uc schema create --catalog main --name default
uc table create --full_name main.default.events \
  --columns "id INT, name STRING" --table_type MANAGED
uc table write --full_name main.default.events   # 15 random rows
uc table read --full_name main.default.events

items.title: 3. Read it from Python
items.text:
from unitycatalog import Client

client = Client("http://localhost:8080/")
table = client.table("main.default.events").get()
print(table.storage_location, [column.name for column in table.columns])

The web UI shows the same table: open main, then default, then events.

items.title: CLI commands
items.text:
Each command of uc is uc <entity> <operation> [flags]. uc <entity> <operation> --help shows the same flags as this page. The flags in bold are required.

Every command also takes the global options:

Option Description --server <url> The server. Default: UC_CLI_SERVER, else cli.server, else http://localhost:8080. --auth_token <token> The token of the requests. Default: UC_CLI_TOKEN, else cli.token, else the sign-in of uc auth login to the server. --output <format> table (the default), json or jsonPretty. --config <file> The settings file, instead of UC_CONFIG or uc.toml.

The list commands take --max_results (default 100) and --page_token. After a full page, uc prints the option for the next page to standard error, such as Next page: --page_token sales. The lists of users and groups page with --start_index: the server gives at most 1000 of them in one page, and uc prints the option for the next page while there are more.

items.title: catalog
items.text:
Operation Flags create --name, --comment, --properties, --storage_root list --max_results, --page_token get --name update --name, and one or more of --new_name, --comment, --properties delete --name, --force (also delete its schemas and what they hold)

--properties is a JSON object: '{"team": "sales"}'.

items.title: schema
items.text: Operation Flags create --catalog, --name, --comment, --properties, --storage_root list --catalog, --max_results, --page_token get --full_name (catalog.schema) update --full_name, and one or more of --new_name, --comment, --properties delete --full_name, --force (also delete what it holds)

items.title: table
items.text:
Operation Flags create --full_name (catalog.schema.table), --columns, --format, --table_type, --storage_location, --properties list --catalog, --schema, --max_results, --page_token get --full_name delete --full_name read --full_name, --max_results (rows; default 100) write --full_name: writes 15 random rows
  • --columns: "id INT, price DECIMAL(10,2)". The types are BOOLEAN, BYTE, SHORT, INT, LONG, FLOAT, DOUBLE, DATE, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMP_NTZ, STRING, BINARY and DECIMAL(p,s). A DECIMAL needs both a precision p from 1 to 38 and a scale s from 0 to p.
  • --format: DELTA (the default), ICEBERG, CSV, JSON, AVRO, PARQUET, ORC, TEXT or LANCE. Only DELTA gets a Delta table at the location; read and write work with Delta tables.
  • --table_type: EXTERNAL (the default), which needs --storage_location, or MANAGED.
  • When a Delta table is already at the location of an EXTERNAL table, create keeps it. --columns must then have its columns, with the same names and types, in the same order.

items.title: user
items.text:
Operation Flags create --name, --email, --external_id list --filter (SCIM, such as 'userName eq "alice@example.com"'), --start_index (from 1), --count (default 100) get --id update --id, --name, --external_id, --email delete --id: deletes the user with its grants, tokens and group memberships; its objects have no owner then

A user's email is its name in grants and owners. update --email replaces the user's primary email and keeps its other emails. It moves the user's grants, owned objects and tokens to the new email. A userName that was the old email changes with it, so the old email is free for another user. A userName from an identity provider stays.

items.title: Helm chart values
items.text:
The values of the Helm chart oci://ghcr.io/open-lakehouse/charts/uc-server. Kubernetes shows them per task. The chart's values.yaml has a comment for each value:

helm show values oci://ghcr.io/open-lakehouse/charts/uc-server --version 0.0.2

The chart sets the server's settings as UC_* environment variables. For the settings without a value here, use server.deployment.env or server.config.toml.

Value Default Description server.enabled true Install the server. server.db.type file file (embedded Turso, one replica) or postgresql. server.db.fileConfig.persistence.enabled true Keep the database on a volume; else an emptyDir. server.db.fileConfig.persistence.pvcName "" The claim's name; default <release>-uc-server-server-db. server.db.fileConfig.persistence.createPVC true Make the claim. server.db.fileConfig.persistence.accessModes ["ReadWriteOnce"] The claim's access modes. server.db.fileConfig.persistence.size 1Gi The claim's size. server.db.fileConfig.persistence.storageClassName "" The claim's storage class. server.db.postgresqlConfig.host "" The PostgreSQL host (required for postgresql). server.db.postgresqlConfig.port 5432 Its port. server.db.postgresqlConfig.dbName ucdb The database. server.db.postgresqlConfig.username postgres The user. server.db.postgresqlConfig.passwordSecretName "" A Secret with the password; no password without it. server.db.postgresqlConfig.passwordSecretKey password The key of the password in that Secret. server.db.postgresqlConfig.ssl.enabled false Use ssl.mode; without it, TLS when offered, unchecked. server.db.postgresqlConfig.ssl.mode verify-full libpq's sslmode: require, verify-ca or verify-full. server.db.postgresqlConfig.ssl.rootCert "" The PEM of the root certificate. server.db.postgresqlConfig.ssl.rootCertConfigMapName "" Or a ConfigMap with it. server.db.postgresqlConfig.ssl.rootCertConfigMapKey ca.crt Its key in the ConfigMap. server.db.postgresqlConfig.extraParams {} More parameters of the connection URL. server.config.toml "" A uc.toml for other settings; the variables win over it. server.service.type ClusterIP The Service's type. server.service.port 8080 The Service's port for the API and the web UI. server.deployment.replicaCount 1 Replicas; above 1 needs postgresql. server.deployment.port 8080 The container's port for the API and the web UI. server.deployment.obsPort 8081 The port of the probes and the metrics. server.deployment.image.repository ghcr.io/open-lakehouse/unitycatalog-rs The image. server.deployment.image.tag "" Its tag; default the chart's appVersion. server.deployment.image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent The pull policy. server.deployment.imagePullSecrets [] Pull secrets. server.deployment.env {} More environment variables, such as UC_* settings. server.deployment.resources {} The container's resources. server.deployment.podSecurityContext user 65532, RuntimeDefault The pod's security context. server.deployment.securityContext read-only root, no capabilities The container's security context. server.deployment.extraVolumes, extraVolumeMounts [] More volumes and mounts. server.deployment.extraInitContainers, extraContainers [] More containers. server.deployment.extraPodAnnotations, extraPodLabels {} More annotations and labels on the pod. server.deployment.nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity empty Scheduling. server.deployment.updateStrategy {} The Deployment's strategy. server.deployment.enableStartupProbe, startupProbe true, {} The startup probe, and its spec instead of the default. server.deployment.enableLivenessProbe, livenessProbe true, {} The liveness probe, the same way. server.deployment.enableReadinessProbe, readinessProbe true, {} The readiness probe, the same way. server.keysSecret.name "" The Secret of the server's keys, private_key.pem (auth.signing_key_file) and secrets_key.pem (secrets.key_file); default <release>-uc-server-server-keys. server.keysSecret.create true Make the Secret at install when it does not exist. server.logLevel info RUST_LOG. auth.enabled false Sign-in and privilege checks. auth.users [] Users that the server makes at start when they are missing: email, name, externalId, privileges (on the metastore). auth.issuers [] The identity providers whose tokens the server takes ([[auth.issuers]]): name, kind, issuer, audiences, accounts, direct, principalClaims, clientClaims, groupsClaim, createUsers, displayName. See Identity providers. auth.oidc.issuer "" The OpenID Connect provider of the web UI's sign-in. auth.oidc.clientSecretName "" A Secret with clientId and clientSecret. auth.oidc.scopes openid email profile The scopes that the server asks for. auth.oidc.endSession false "Log out" ends the provider's session too. auth.publicUrl "" The server's URL, for the provider's redirects after sign-in and "Log out". auth.trustedProxies "" The proxies in front of the server that add the client's address to X-Forwarded-For, such as the ingress controller: CIDRs or addresses. The limits per client count by that address. auth.forward.trustedProxies "" The auth proxies' CIDRs or addresses. auth.forward.emailHeader Remote-Email The header with the user's email. auth.forward.userHeader Remote-User The header with the user, without the email header. auth.forward.namesWithCommas false A header value with a , is one name, such as the subject of a client certificate. Only for a proxy that replaces the client's headers. auth.forward.logoutUrl "" The proxy's sign-out, for the web UI's "Log out". auth.opa.url "" Open Policy Agent decides each privilege, OWNER and the admin: the URL of the policy's decision in OPA's data API, such as http://opa:8181/v1/data/uc/authz. Needs auth.enabled. See Open Policy Agent. auth.opa.timeout 5s How long one OPA decision may take. auth.opa.tokenSecretName "" A secret with token: the token that the server sends to OPA, for an OPA that takes tokens. Needs auth.opa.url. See Protect OPA. auth.cookieTimeout 5d The life of the web UI's sign-in. auth.accessTokenTimeout 24h The life of the server's tokens. storage.tableStorageRoot "" Where managed tables go when their catalog and schema have no storage root. storage.modelStorageRoot "" The same for models. storage.identity.aws empty The server's AWS identity: credentialsSecretName (accessKey, secretKey), region, arn, endpoint. Empty: the pod's identity. storage.identity.azure empty The server's Azure identity: credentialsSecretName (directoryId, applicationId, clientSecret) or managedIdentityId. Empty: the pod's identity. storage.identity.gcp empty The server's GCP identity: credentialsSecretName (jsonKey). Empty: the pod's identity. storage.locations [] Per location: url, and one identity of its cloud: awsIamRoleArn (with an optional region), azureManagedIdentity or gcpServiceAccount (true for the server's own identity, or a role ARN, a resource ID or an email), or credentialsSecretName (abfss: directoryId, applicationId, clientSecret; gs: jsonKey). ui.enabled true Serve the web UI at /. ingress.enabled, host, ingressClassName, annotations, tlsSecretName off An Ingress to the server. httpRoute.enabled, host, parentRefs, annotations off An HTTPRoute to the server; parentRefs is required. serviceAccount.create, name, annotations, automount off The pod's ServiceAccount. nameOverride, fullnameOverride "" Other names for the chart's objects.

items.title: HTTP API
items.text: The operations of the server's HTTP APIs, with their parameters, request bodies and responses: the Unity Catalog REST API, the Delta REST API, the Iceberg REST catalog, the control plane and the sharing protocols (Delta Sharing and Open Sharing). Scalar shows them from the OpenAPI document. It comes from the protos in proto/ that the server's routes and the clients follow, and for the sharing protocols from the OpenAPI document of the opensharing-api crate, which serves them.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
uc-server and uc read the same settings. Each setting is a key in a [group] table of uc.toml, and an environment variable UC_<GROUP>_<KEY>: enabled in [auth] is UC_AUTH_ENABLED.

# uc.toml
[server]
data_dir = "/var/lib/uc"

[db]
url = "postgresql://uc@postgres.example.com:5432/uc?sslmode=verify-full"

[auth]
enabled = true
admin_principals = ["alice@example.com"]

The same with variables:

export UC_SERVER_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/uc
export UC_DB_URL='postgresql://uc@postgres.example.com:5432/uc?sslmode=verify-full'
export UC_AUTH_ENABLED=true
export UC_AUTH_ADMIN_PRINCIPALS=alice@example.com

items.title: Where the settings come from
items.text:
A setting takes its value from the first of:

  1. a command-line flag, such as --port;
  2. its environment variable;
  3. uc.toml;
  4. its default.

The settings file is the file of --config, else the file that UC_CONFIG names, else the first uc.toml in the working directory or a folder above it. Without a file, the variables and the defaults apply.

items.title: Values
items.text:
• A key that is not a setting is an error, in the file and in a variable of a group. Errors name the setting, its variable and the file: auth.enabld (UC_AUTH_ENABLD): unknown field.
  • Other UC_ variables are not settings, such as UC_CONFIG.
  • Variables are text. The server reads numbers and booleans from the text. An empty variable is unset.
  • A duration is text such as 30s, 5m, 24h or 5d.
  • A list is a TOML array, or text with commas: UC_AUTH_ADMIN_PRINCIPALS=alice@example.com,bob@example.com.

items.title: Cloud identities and locations
items.text:
[identity.<cloud>] is how the server signs in to AWS, Azure or GCP. A [locations.<name>] gives the paths under its URL an identity, when no external location covers them. Cloud storage tells how they work with external locations, with examples per cloud.

The variables of these tables include the cloud or the name: UC_IDENTITY_AWS_SECRET_KEY is secret_key in [identity.aws], and UC_LOCATIONS_ANALYTICS_URL is url in [locations.analytics]. A name has only lowercase letters and digits, and at least one letter: the server reads a name of only digits, such as UC_LOCATIONS_0_URL, as a list index.

items.title: [server]
items.text: Setting Variable Default Description Where it runs Its database folder and its address. data_dir UC_SERVER_DATA_DIR .uc The folder of the embedded database, unless db.url names another database. bind UC_SERVER_BIND 0.0.0.0:8080 The address of the APIs and the web UI. --port changes its port. Requests Limits on the requests that it serves. max_request_length UC_SERVER_MAX_REQUEST_LENGTH 10485760 The largest request body, in bytes. A larger one gets 413. Not for uploads to the Files API, which stream to storage. request_timeout UC_SERVER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT 10s The time that a request can take; then the server answers 503. 0s for no limit. Not for uploads and directory deletes of the Files API. rate_limit_per_sec UC_SERVER_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC 0 Requests per second from one client address; more get 429. 0 for no limit. Behind a proxy, set auth.trusted_proxies, else all callers are one client. cors_allow_origins UC_SERVER_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS all origins The origins that browsers can call the API from. Empty or * allows every origin. Health checks and metrics /livez, /readyz and /metrics. obs_port UC_SERVER_OBS_PORT none The port of /livez, /readyz and /metrics, on all interfaces. Not the API's port. readiness_interval UC_SERVER_READINESS_INTERVAL 5s How often /readyz checks the database. readiness_db_timeout UC_SERVER_READINESS_DB_TIMEOUT 2s How long that check can take. Threads The threads that serve requests and outbound IO. workers UC_SERVER_WORKERS one per CPU The threads that serve requests. Each has a runtime of its own and its share of the PostgreSQL connections (db.pool_size), so a request runs on one thread. io_threads UC_SERVER_IO_THREADS 1 The threads for outbound IO: the connections to object stores and HTTP services.

items.title: [db]
items.text: Setting Variable Default Description url UC_DB_URL uc.db in data_dir; uc dev: memory file:<path>, memory, postgresql://… or jdbc:postgresql://…. See Database. user UC_DB_USER from the URL The PostgreSQL user, instead of the URL's. password UC_DB_PASSWORD from the URL The PostgreSQL password, instead of the URL's. pool_size UC_DB_POOL_SIZE 20 The most PostgreSQL connections at one time.

items.title: [auth]
items.text: Setting Variable Default Description Authorization Sign-in and privilege checks for the API, and the first users and admins. enabled UC_AUTH_ENABLED false Require sign-in, and check privileges. admin_principals UC_AUTH_ADMIN_PRINCIPALS none The emails of the admins, besides the metastore's owner: see Privileges. users none none [[auth.users]]: the users that the server makes at each start when they are missing. Only in uc.toml. See The first users. engine UC_AUTH_ENGINE grants What decides each privilege: grants, cedar (see Cedar policies) or opa (see Open Policy Agent). cedar and opa need enabled = true. cedar_policies UC_AUTH_CEDAR_POLICIES none With engine = "cedar": files of Cedar policies, on top of the default policy. opa_url UC_AUTH_OPA_URL none With engine = "opa": the URL of the policy's decision in OPA's data API, such as http://opa:8181/v1/data/uc/authz. opa_timeout UC_AUTH_OPA_TIMEOUT 5s With engine = "opa": how long one decision may take. opa_token_file UC_AUTH_OPA_TOKEN_FILE none With engine = "opa": a file with the token that the server sends to OPA as Authorization: Bearer <token>, for an OPA that takes tokens. See Protect OPA. trusted_proxies UC_AUTH_TRUSTED_PROXIES none The proxies in front of the server that add the client's address to X-Forwarded-For, such as an ingress: CIDRs or addresses. The limits per client count by that address. See Behind a proxy. Tokens The server's own tokens, and the identity providers whose tokens it takes. signing_key_file UC_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY_FILE none The PEM file of the RSA keys of the server's tokens, newest first: the first signs. Without it, the server makes a key in memory at each start. See The signing key. access_token_timeout UC_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TIMEOUT 24h The life of the server's access tokens. cookie_timeout UC_AUTH_COOKIE_TIMEOUT 5d The life of the UC_TOKEN cookie of the web UI. issuers none none [[auth.issuers]]: the identity providers whose tokens the server takes, at the token exchange and, with direct, on every request. Only in uc.toml. The keys follow. Web UI sign-in How users sign in to the web UI. The settings of each mode follow. mode UC_AUTH_MODE none The web UI's sign-in: none, oidc or forward. OpenID Connect mode = "oidc": the server signs users in with an OpenID Connect provider. public_url UC_AUTH_PUBLIC_URL none The server's external URL. The provider returns the browser to <public_url>/auth/callback, and with oidc_end_session to <public_url>/ after "Log out". The URLs in SCIM answers and Delta Sharing profiles start with it, in every mode; without it, they start with the URL that the client called. oidc_issuer UC_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER none The OpenID Connect provider's issuer. oidc_client_id UC_AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_ID none The OAuth client. oidc_client_secret UC_AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET none Its secret; none for a public client. oidc_scopes UC_AUTH_OIDC_SCOPES openid email profile The scopes that the server asks for. oidc_end_session UC_AUTH_OIDC_END_SESSION false "Log out" also ends the provider's session: see OpenID Connect. Auth proxy mode = "forward": an auth proxy in front of the server signs users in, and sends their email in a header. forward_trusted_proxies UC_AUTH_FORWARD_TRUSTED_PROXIES none The auth proxies whose headers count: CIDRs or addresses. forward_email_header UC_AUTH_FORWARD_EMAIL_HEADER Remote-Email The header with the user's email. forward_user_header UC_AUTH_FORWARD_USER_HEADER Remote-User The header with the user, without the email header. forward_names_with_commas UC_AUTH_FORWARD_NAMES_WITH_COMMAS false A header value with a , is one name, such as the subject of a client certificate (CN=alice,OU=eng). Without it, such a value names nobody, as it could be the client's value with the proxy's added. Set it only when the proxy replaces the client's headers. forward_logout_url UC_AUTH_FORWARD_LOGOUT_URL none The proxy's sign-out, where the web UI's "Log out" goes.

items.title: [[auth.issuers]]
items.text:
[[auth.issuers]]
name = "entra"
issuer = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0"
audiences = ["<the API app's client id>", "https://uc.example.com"]
direct = true
principal_claims = ["preferred_username", "oid"]
client_claims = ["azp", "appid"]
groups_claim = "roles"
create_users = true
display_name = "{app_displayname}"
Key Default Description name required A short name of lowercase letters, digits, - and _: the prefix of the principals it names without an email, such as entra:<oid>. kind oidc oidc for an OpenID Connect provider; aws for AWS identities, whose signed GetCallerIdentity requests the server sends to STS. issuer required The iss claim of its tokens, as they write it, with a trailing / if they have one; * stands for one DNS label of letters, digits and -, and in the host it needs two fixed labels after it. For aws, the URL of the STS endpoint, by default AWS's global and regional ones. audiences required The aud that its tokens must carry; ["*"] accepts every audience, without direct; with direct, no *. For aws, the server id that the signed requests carry: the server's URL as clients call it; no *. Clients ask for the audience that is the server's URL. accounts required for aws The 12-digit AWS accounts whose identities it takes. direct false Take its tokens on every request, not only at the token exchange. principal_claims ["email", "sub"] The claims that name the caller; the first present wins. An email names the user with that email; with an issuer with *, only when the token says email_verified = true. Any other value names the user <name>:<value>. client_claims ["azp", "client_id"] The claims with an application's client id: the user whose externalId is <name>:<client id> is the application. groups_claim none A claim whose values are names of groups the caller is in; a value counts when the server has the group <name>:<value>, such as entra:Writers. Not with an issuer that has *. create_users false Make the user at its first request when it is missing. display_name the principal The display name of a made user, with claims in braces.

Identity providers tells how a block names the caller.

Sign-in and authorization tells how these settings work together.

items.title: [storage]
items.text: Setting Variable Default Description Managed storage Where managed tables and models go by default. tables_root UC_STORAGE_TABLES_ROOT none; uc dev: storage in its --dir Where managed tables go when their catalog and schema have no storage root. models_root UC_STORAGE_MODELS_ROOT none; uc dev: storage in its --dir Where models go when their catalog and schema have no storage root. Local external tables Local folders for external Iceberg tables. external_local_roots UC_STORAGE_EXTERNAL_LOCAL_ROOTS none The local folders under which external Iceberg tables can be. Cleanup of dropped data When you delete a managed table, volume or model, the server deletes its files later. cleanup_initial_delay UC_STORAGE_CLEANUP_INITIAL_DELAY 7d How long the server waits before it deletes the data of a dropped object. cleanup_retry_backoff UC_STORAGE_CLEANUP_RETRY_BACKOFF 1h The wait before a failed cleanup runs again. cleanup_poll_interval UC_STORAGE_CLEANUP_POLL_INTERVAL 1m How often the cleanup of dropped managed data looks for work. cleanup_attempt_timeout UC_STORAGE_CLEANUP_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT 30m How long one cleanup can take. cleanup_lease_duration UC_STORAGE_CLEANUP_LEASE_DURATION 2h How long a server holds a cleanup task. Credential cache Vended credentials given again in place of a new call to the cloud. See The credential cache. credential_cache_enabled UC_STORAGE_CREDENTIAL_CACHE_ENABLED false Give a vended credential again to requests for the same locations, operation and identity. credential_cache_max_size UC_STORAGE_CREDENTIAL_CACHE_MAX_SIZE 1000 The most credentials kept. credential_cache_max_age UC_STORAGE_CREDENTIAL_CACHE_MAX_AGE 5m The longest a credential is given again, from when it was vended.

items.title: [secrets]
items.text: Setting Variable Default Description store UC_SECRETS_STORE database Where the secrets of credentials go. database: in the database, sealed with key_file. key_file UC_SECRETS_KEY_FILE none The PEM file of the P-256 keys that seal the secrets, newest first. Without it, the server makes a new key in memory at each start, so the secrets cannot be opened after it stops. See The secrets key. cache_capacity UC_SECRETS_CACHE_CAPACITY 500 The most secrets, and Azure sign-ins, that the server keeps in memory. 0 keeps none. cache_ttl UC_SECRETS_CACHE_TTL 10m How long a secret stays in memory after the store gives it.

items.title: [tables]
items.text: Setting Variable Default Description managed UC_TABLES_MANAGED true Allow MANAGED tables, staging tables and Delta commits. delta_api_only UC_TABLES_DELTA_API_ONLY false Write managed Delta tables only through the Delta REST API. allow_missing_deletion_vectors UC_TABLES_ALLOW_MISSING_DELETION_VECTORS false Allow UniForm Iceberg v2 tables without deletion vectors. iceberg_writes UC_TABLES_ICEBERG_WRITES true Allow writes through the Iceberg REST catalog.

items.title: [identity.aws]
items.text:
The identity that the server signs in to AWS with. It assumes the roles of storage credentials. Without keys, the server uses the credentials of the machine or pod where it runs: the AWS_* variables, the role of a Kubernetes service account, an ECS task role, EKS Pod Identity or an instance role.

Setting Variable Default Description access_key UC_IDENTITY_AWS_ACCESS_KEY the credentials where the server runs The access key. secret_key UC_IDENTITY_AWS_SECRET_KEY the credentials where the server runs The secret key. region UC_IDENTITY_AWS_REGION AWS_REGION, else AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, else us-east-1 The region of the STS calls. arn UC_IDENTITY_AWS_ARN none The ARN of this identity, shown as unity_catalog_iam_arn on storage credentials, for the trust policies of their roles. A role here is also the one of aws_iam_role_arn = true; its trust policy must then allow the role itself. endpoint UC_IDENTITY_AWS_ENDPOINT AWS The S3 and STS API of an S3-compatible store, such as MinIO or RustFS: http:// or https://. uc's table and volume commands use it too. See Cloud storage.

items.title: [identity.azure]
items.text:
The identity that the server signs in to Azure with: a service principal, or a user-assigned managed identity. Without one, the server uses the credentials of the machine or pod where it runs: AKS workload identity, the AZURE_* variables, or the managed identity of the VM or App Service.

Setting Variable Description directory_id UC_IDENTITY_AZURE_DIRECTORY_ID The service principal's tenant ID. application_id UC_IDENTITY_AZURE_APPLICATION_ID The service principal's client ID. client_secret UC_IDENTITY_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET The service principal's secret. managed_identity_id UC_IDENTITY_AZURE_MANAGED_IDENTITY_ID Or the resource ID of a user-assigned managed identity, from the instance metadata service.

items.title: [identity.gcp]
items.text:
The identity that the server signs in to GCP with. Without a key, the server uses the credentials of the machine or pod where it runs, which Google calls Application Default Credentials: the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS file, gcloud's application default credentials, or the metadata server, such as GKE Workload Identity.

Setting Variable Default Description json_key_file UC_IDENTITY_GCP_JSON_KEY_FILE Application Default Credentials A service account's JSON key file. endpoint UC_IDENTITY_GCP_ENDPOINT Google The STS and IAM Credentials API of a GCP emulator, such as Floci: http:// or https://.

items.title: [locations.<name>]
items.text:
A URL and the identity that reaches the paths under it, for paths that no external location covers. With authorization on, it serves only the paths that the admin wrote, storage.tables_root and storage.models_root; see Which location serves a path. The URL's scheme picks the cloud, and an entry holds exactly one identity of that cloud. When several entries cover a path, the one with the longest URL wins.

Setting Variable Cloud Description url UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_URL all s3://bucket, abfss://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net or gs://bucket, with a path or without. Required. region UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_REGION S3 The bucket's region, which Iceberg clients get. Without it, the server asks S3. aws_iam_role_arn UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_AWS_IAM_ROLE_ARN S3 true for the server's own role, identity.aws.arn, or the ARN of a role that [identity.aws] assumes. Required for S3. azure_directory_id UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_AZURE_DIRECTORY_ID ADLS A service principal's tenant ID, with azure_application_id and azure_client_secret. azure_application_id UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_AZURE_APPLICATION_ID ADLS Its client ID. azure_client_secret UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET ADLS Its secret. azure_managed_identity UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_AZURE_MANAGED_IDENTITY ADLS true for [identity.azure], or the resource ID of a user-assigned managed identity. gcp_service_account UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT GCS true for [identity.gcp], or the email of a service account that [identity.gcp] impersonates. gcp_service_account_key UC_LOCATIONS_<NAME>_GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY GCS A service account's JSON key file.

One update action. The action says which fields are set: - set-properties: updates, property names to string values. - remove-properties: removals. - set-columns: columns. - set-table-comment: comment. - add-commit: commit and uniform. - set-latest-backfilled-version: latest_published_version. - set-protocol: protocol. - set-domain-metadata: updates, domain names to their metadata: delta.clustering to {"clusteringColumns": [["a"], ["b", "c"]]}, delta.rowTracking to {"rowIdHighWaterMark": 9}. - remove-domain-metadata: domains. - set-partition-columns: partition_columns. - update-metadata-snapshot-version: last_commit_version and last_commit_timestamp_ms.

items.text:
The token providers of cloud identities, for Client(url, token_provider=...).

Each function makes a TokenProvider in Rust that gets a token when the client first sends a request, and a new one before it expires. Client(url) without a token calls detect itself, so a program names a provider only to choose one.

Classes

Name Description TokenProvider A token provider made in Rust, for token_provider=. The binding crate makes one from any olai_http::RequestSigner, such as a bearer provider in a BearerProviderSigner.

items.title: aws(server_id: str) → TokenProvider
items.text: An AWS identity of the environment, for the server whose AWS issuer block has the audience server_id, such as https://uc.example.com. Each token is a signed GetCallerIdentity request, which the server sends to STS: the credentials stay here. They are the access keys of AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (with AWS_SESSION_TOKEN), a web identity (AWS_ROLE_ARN, AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE), the container's credentials, else the instance role of the machine.

items.title: unitycatalog
items.text:
Python client for unitycatalog-rs, the Rust reimplementation of Unity Catalog OSS.

Client wraps the Rust uc-client. It takes the root URL of the server. Each method comes twice: name waits for the response, and name_async returns an awaitable. The requests on one catalog, schema, table and so on are on its handle, such as client.catalog("main"):

import asyncio
from unitycatalog import Client

client = Client("http://localhost:8080/")
client.create_catalog("main", comment="primary")
print([c.name for c in client.list_catalogs()])

async def main():
    catalog = await client.catalog("main").get_async()
    print(catalog.id)

asyncio.run(main())

The classes of the requests and responses are in a module per API package, such as unitycatalog.tables, with the enums of that package. Enums are enum.StrEnum classes; a parameter takes a member or its name. An error answer raises UnityCatalogError, or the subclass of its HTTP status, such as NotFoundError.

With sign-in, Client(url, token=...) sends a fixed token, and Client(url) signs in with the identity of the environment: an Azure or Google identity, an OAuth client, or a token in UC_TOKEN. Client(url, token_provider=...) names the token source: one of unitycatalog.identity, or a callable that returns the token.

Classes

Name Description BadRequestError The server answered 400 Bad Request: the request is not valid. Client A client of the API at one base URL. ConflictError The server answered 409 Conflict: the resource exists or changed. NotFoundError The server answered 404 Not Found: the resource does not exist. PermissionDeniedError The server answered 403 Forbidden: the caller may not do this. RateLimitError The server answered 429 Too Many Requests. ServerError The server answered with a 5xx status: it failed to do the request. UnauthenticatedError The server answered 401 Unauthorized: the request has no valid credentials. UnityCatalogError An error answer of the server, or a request that got no answer.
